issues.t: Misfire from worn valve seats in the cylinder head
issues.sym: A flashing or steady check engine light, rough idle, shaking, poor acceleration and worse fuel economy. Codes often point to one cylinder, commonly No. 2, 3 or 5.
issues.why: The exhaust valve seats in the 5-cylinder engine’s aluminum head wear or recede, so a valve no longer seals and the cylinder loses compression. It is the best-known H3 engine problem and some heads were replaced under warranty.
issues.next: Have a compression or leak-down test done to confirm it. A new or rebuilt cylinder head is the usual fix; a head swap can fail again if the root cause is not addressed, so use a shop that knows these engines.

issues.t: Blower motor connector can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell from behind the glove box, smoke, the fan working only on some speeds, or melted wiring at the blower resistor.
issues.why: The module that controls blower fan speed and its connector can overheat, melting the wiring and creating a fire risk. GM recalled 2006-2010 H3 and 2009-2010 H3T trucks to replace part of the connector and harness.
issues.next: Have a GM dealer run your VIN and do the free recall repair. If the fan acts up or you smell burning plastic, turn the fan off until it is fixed.

issues.t: Hood louver can come loose and fly off (recall)
issues.sym: A rattle from the hood vent at speed, and in some reports the plastic hood louver breaking free and hitting the windshield.
issues.why: Clips holding the decorative louver to the hood can break. GM recalled the trucks to glue the louver in place, but some owners say it came off again later.
issues.next: Make sure the recall is done, and check the louver for looseness after car washes or off-road trips.

issues.t: H3T fuel tank front strap can break (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning; a broken strap may cause a clunk or the tank sitting lower than normal.
issues.why: On some 2009 H3T pickups, the front fuel tank strap could crack. If the rear strap and shield also failed, the tank could drop. GM recalled these trucks for a new strap.
issues.next: Have a dealer check your VIN. The new-design strap is installed free.

issues.t: Radiator plastic tank cracks and leaks coolant
issues.sym: Coolant drips or puddles under the front, a sweet smell, the low coolant light, or the engine overheating.
issues.why: The plastic tanks on the H3’s radiator crack, often at the top. It is one of the most-reported H3 repairs in owner surveys, on both the 5-cylinder and V8.
issues.next: Keep an eye on the coolant level and temperature gauge. Replace a cracked radiator before it overheats the engine, which can ruin the cylinder head.

issues.t: Water pump leaks or fails
issues.sym: Coolant leaking near the front of the engine, a whining or grinding noise, or overheating.
issues.why: The water pump bearing or seal wears out. Several 3.7L owners report replacing it at roughly 55,000 to 120,000 miles.
issues.next: Replace a leaking pump soon; overheating is especially hard on this engine’s cylinder head.

issues.t: Thermostat sticks (overheating or check engine light)
issues.sym: The temperature gauge runs high or low, the heater is weak, or the check engine light comes on.
issues.why: The thermostat can stick open or closed. Owners of several H3 years report replacing it for overheating or a check engine light.
issues.next: Have the cooling system checked; a bad thermostat is a small fix compared with the damage overheating can do.

issues.t: Check engine light from gas cap or EVAP valve
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with no change in how the truck drives, sometimes coming back after a new gas cap.
issues.why: A worn gas cap seal or a failed EVAP vent solenoid or canister lets fuel vapor escape, which the computer reads as a leak.
issues.next: Tighten or replace the gas cap first. If the light returns, have the EVAP system smoke-tested to find the leak.

issues.t: Will not start, security light on (theft-system lockout)
issues.sym: The truck cranks but will not start or will not crank, a security or anti-theft light or message appears, and it starts again after waiting 10 to 20 minutes.
issues.why: The theft-deterrent system loses the signal from the ignition lock cylinder and disables starting. A worn lock cylinder or switch is often blamed.
issues.next: Leave the key on for about 10 minutes until the security light goes off, then try again. Have a shop check the ignition lock cylinder and theft system for a lasting fix.

issues.t: Fuel pump failure (stalls or will not start)
issues.sym: The engine cranks but will not start, or it shuts off while driving; you may not hear the pump hum when the key is turned on.
issues.why: The in-tank fuel pump or its relay fails. Some owners also report rusted pump and tank parts.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Have fuel pressure tested to confirm the pump is the cause before replacing it.

issues.t: Side curtain airbags deploy without a crash
issues.sym: Side curtain airbags go off while driving slowly over rough ground or with no impact at all.
issues.why: Owners report the rollover/side-impact sensing system firing the curtain airbags when it should not. The cause was not confirmed.
issues.next: Report it to NHTSA and the dealer. Replacing deployed airbags and sensors is a major repair, so check with your insurer.

issues.t: Sunroof drains clog and leak water inside
issues.sym: Wet headliner, water on the seats or floor, musty smell, or warning lights after rain.
issues.why: The sunroof drain tubes plug up and water overflows into the cabin. Water reaching wiring and sensors can set ABS or stability control warnings.
issues.next: Clear the sunroof drains regularly. Dry wet carpet quickly to avoid mold and electrical damage.

issues.t: Rear leaf spring cracks or breaks
issues.sym: A bang or clunk from the rear, the truck leaning to one side, or the rear wheel shifting and wobbling.
issues.why: The rear leaf springs can crack near their front mounting eye, especially when rust has weakened the mounts.
issues.next: Have the springs and mounts inspected if the rear sits unevenly. Replace springs in pairs.

issues.t: Frame and spring mount rust
issues.sym: Visible scaling rust on the frame, rotted spring mounts, or holes in the frame near the rear axle.
issues.why: Owners in salt-belt states report the frame and rear spring mounts rusting badly enough to worry about the axle or frame failing.
issues.next: Have the frame inspected before buying an older H3. Severe frame rust can make the truck unsafe and hard to repair.

issues.t: Broken exhaust manifold bolts on the V8
issues.sym: A ticking exhaust leak on startup, an exhaust smell, and in one report exhaust fumes in the cabin.
issues.why: Bolts holding the exhaust manifolds on the 5.3L V8 can snap from repeated heating and cooling.
issues.next: Fix exhaust leaks promptly, especially if you smell fumes inside, since exhaust contains carbon monoxide.

issues.t: Catalytic converter bracket or bolts break
issues.sym: A rattle or exhaust leak noise from under the truck, sometimes with a check engine light.
issues.why: On the 5-cylinder, the catalytic converter bracket and bolts can break; one owner also had bolts snap in the head and needed a new head and converter.
issues.next: Have broken brackets fixed early so the exhaust is not hanging on the manifold studs.

issues.t: V8 lifter or bearing failure
issues.sym: Ticking or knocking from the engine, a misfire, or metal in the oil.
issues.why: Owners of the 5.3L V8 report a stuck lifter that damaged the camshaft and a spun main bearing, both requiring an engine replacement.
issues.next: Stop driving if you hear knocking and have the oil checked for metal. Regular oil changes with the right oil help protect the lifters.

issues.t: Front wheel bearing wear
issues.sym: A humming or growling noise that grows with speed, a loose feel in the steering, or an ABS light.
issues.why: Front wheel bearing and hub assemblies are among the most common H3 repairs reported by owners.
issues.next: Have the noise checked. Replace a failing bearing before it gets loose enough to affect steering.

issues.t: CV axle or joint wear (clicking on turns)
issues.sym: Clicking or popping when turning, vibration, or grease thrown around the inside of the wheel.
issues.why: The front CV axles and joints wear out, often after a torn boot lets dirt in. They are one of the more common H3 repairs.
issues.next: Inspect CV boots at each oil change; a torn boot caught early can save the axle.

issues.t: Heater or A/C controls stop adjusting temperature
issues.sym: Temperature will not change, the A/C does not cool, or the climate control buttons and lights stop working.
issues.why: The climate control head or its module fails. Some owners also need A/C expansion valves.
issues.next: Have the HVAC system scanned. The control head is often the fix if the blower works but the temperature will not change.

issues.t: Camshaft sensor or cam timing codes
issues.sym: Check engine light with cam timing or sensor codes, sometimes rough running.
issues.why: The camshaft position sensor or the cam timing (phaser) solenoid can fail on the 5-cylinder engines.
issues.next: Check the oil level and change the oil if it is old, since cam timing parts rely on clean oil. Then have the sensor or solenoid tested.

issues.t: 4WD transfer case will not shift
issues.sym: The 4WD will not engage or disengage, or the drivetrain locks up.
issues.why: The transfer case shift motor can fail, and one owner reported a plastic shift fork breaking.
issues.next: Have the 4WD system scanned. A shift motor is a far simpler fix than internal transfer case repairs.

issues.t: Battery drains overnight (door switch or seat button)
issues.sym: A dead battery after the truck sits, interior lights or the info display staying on, or doors showing open when closed.
issues.why: A corroded door switch can keep lights and modules awake, and a cracked seat trim piece pressing a power seat button drained one owner’s battery.
issues.next: Watch whether the dome light or door-ajar message stays on. Clean or replace the faulty door switch and test for a parasitic drain.

issues.t: Fuel gauge reads empty after filling
issues.sym: The fuel gauge shows low or empty right after a fill-up, then reads normally later.
issues.why: The fuel level sender in the tank or its circuit gives a bad reading.
issues.next: Track mileage between fill-ups until it is fixed so you do not run out of fuel.
